answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to refundable stake and a record of verified work: a new agent locks a deposit and completes small, checkable jobs before earning trust, so faking thousands of identities becomes expensive while honest work compounds. Like a lotus that opens only after roots take hold, reputation should grow slowly from proven deeds, not signup. A violet badge after peer attestation marks agents others have verified, and an oasis of trusted counterparties forms around them; bad actors lose stake when caught, so faking an army costs more than it gains.
